name: Vibrant Purple
lede: Vibrant Purple is a descriptive name for a saturated purple; in chemistry books the same two words describe the color of a dye forming in a flask.

sections.title: A survey name
sections.body: The name is a modifier plus a basic color word, and the library's only source for it is the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS category is vivid purple, about 8 units away [1]. In printed English the phrase is almost absent before 1980 and climbs steeply from about 2000 [2]. Close neighbors are [[dark-orchid]], [[vivid-purple]] and [[bright-purple]] [3].

sections.title: Purple in the flask
sections.body: Garfield gives a laboratory recipe for remaking [[mauve]]: very soon after potassium dichromate is added, the solution turns a vibrant purple [4]. Garfield also notes a modern forensic test in which a diazo dye, added to a sample, produces the same kind of vibrant purple [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, within a distance of 4 units, as photographed [6]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole, and photographs of varnished paintings are not pigment tests.
